findings.where: packages/runtime/lib/knowledge-retrieval.mjs:174-188 (the core_readable/core_unreadable branch in retrieveKnowledge); packages/db/migrations/0230_knowledge_retrieval.sql:401-412 (clara.retrieve_knowledge's only return jsonb_build_object(...))
findings.what: The runtime module checks answer.core_readable !== false and, when false, returns a distinct unavailable("core_unreadable", ...) result, and successor-contract stanza (A) in reports/658-final.md describes the v5 terminal as firing 'when faceStatusOf is unknown/denied with reason core_unreadable, refused or read_failed on the core arm' as though core_unreadable is a live outcome. But clara.retrieve_knowledge is a single atomic PL/pgSQL statement (0230:265-413) with no code path that ever sets a core_readable key on its one success return, and any internal failure raises an exception the caller already maps to unavailable("refused"/"read_failed", ...) two lines above the core_readable check. So core_unreadable can never actually be produced by the shipped door -- it is unreachable outside a hand-built test fixture.
findings.evidence: grep -rn "core_readable" packages/ apps/ returns exactly three lines: the comment and the check in knowledge-retrieval.mjs, and one synthetic literal in packages/runtime/tests/knowledge-retrieval.test.mjs:134 ({ ...ANSWER, core_readable: false }) that manually fabricates the field rather than obtaining it from a real door call. Reading the full body of clara.retrieve_knowledge (0230_knowledge_retrieval.sql:265-413) confirms its only successful return path builds jsonb_build_object('status','ok', 'client_id', ..., 'records', v_records) with no core_readable key anywhere, and the function has no partial-failure path (core, requested and remainder are computed by one CTE chain in one statement, so a failure fails the whole call, which the exception handler in knowledge-retrieval.mjs already routes to unavailable("refused")/unavailable("read_failed") before the core_readable check is ever reached).
findings.fix: Either remove the core_readable/core_unreadable branch as dead code and note in the module header that D16's core-tier terminal fires on ANY unavailable result (the atomic door cannot fail partially, so 'core unreadable' and 'the whole read failed' are the same event today), or, if a future door revision is meant to signal a core-only failure independently, say so explicitly so the v5-cut integrator does not assume core_unreadable is already reachable. Behaviourally this is benign -- every real failure still stops the Work via the same fail-closed paths -- so it does not block acceptance.
